identification.name: Aluminum 6061-T6
identification.common_form_notes: Widely stocked in most metals suppliers. Extrusions available in many standard profiles.
identification.notes: T6 temper denotes solution heat-treated and artificially aged. One of the most commonly used aluminum alloys in mechanical design. Mechanical properties from MIL-HDBK-5J (U.S. Military Handbook 5J, freely available); AZoM article linked for cross-reference. Cryogenic CTE (coefficient of thermal expansion) table entries (−196 to −100 °C) are instantaneous values from the NIST (National Institute of Standards and Technology) Cryogenic Materials Database polynomial for 6061-T6 (underlying data: Mann, NBS (National Bureau of Standards, NIST's predecessor agency), 1977; ±4% accuracy). Above-RT CTE entries from MIL-HDBK-5J. Ductility (min 8%) is the MIL-HDBK-5J minimum specification for thicker product forms; AA typical values are 12% (round bar ≥12.7 mm) to 17% (sheet ≤1.59 mm) per MatWeb. Melting point is solidus (582°C); liquidus 652°C (MIL-HDBK-5J). Fatigue S-N curve (4 points, R=−1 fully reversed) is Yahr (1993, ORNL/ASME) — the best-fit curve to fully-reversed 6061-T6 fatigue data compiled from 5 literature sources (Structural Alloys Handbook 1989, Alcoa Structural Handbook 1960, MIL-HDBK-5D 1984, AFML-TDR-64-280 1970, Brodrick & Spiering 1972): S = 14,479/√N + 96.5 MPa. This is the raw best-fit curve, NOT the paper's safety-factored nuclear-pressure-vessel design curve (which reduces stress by 2× or life by 20× for code allowables) — using the design curve here would misrepresent the material's actual fatigue behavior as far worse than reality. Test method is left undocumented (not null-by-default — genuinely mixed): the paper states low-cycle data (<10³ cycles) is axial strain-controlled while some high-cycle data is rotating-beam, merged into one fit; at the life range stored here (≥1e5 cycles, well within the paper's stated elastic regime) the distinction matters less, but a single test_method can't be honestly assigned. Replaces a previously stored MIL-HDBK-5J-cited curve (150/130/110/97 MPa) that did not reproduce MIL-HDBK-5J's own rod/bar equation (Figure 3.6.2.2.8) at any consistent R when back-solved (implied R ranged from −2.69 to −0.29 across the 4 points) — its actual origin was unknown, so it was discarded.

typical_usage: Structural frames and enclosures, aircraft components and skin panels, marine fittings, bicycle frames, electronic chassis and heat sinks, machined precision parts. Chosen for its excellent balance of strength, machinability, weldability, and corrosion resistance.
